segments.english: The first: there is a great difference between one who worships and prays to something, and one who only honours something. To pray to something and to worship something with worship is forbidden to us, whether it be a man or an angel, corporeal or spiritual; but to bestow honour, as a youth honours an elder and a servant his master, and it is permitted for the lowly to the honoured. So too we find of our father Abraham, who believed in the LORD, that he shattered the idol-monuments and disowned them, and bowed down to the ground before three angels standing over him, even though they appeared to him as men. So too Joshua did at Jericho: when he saw a man standing before him and took him for an angel, he fell to the ground before him. And if men of heart like them, in whose ways we walk and whose commandments of their lips we do not shrink from, did this, and it was not counted to them as a sin of idolatry; it is clear that to honour a Torah scroll is not the worship of idols.

grammar: בין ... ובין frames the contrast: the second half is elliptical, so 'one who only honours' is set against 'one who worships and prays'.
ולעבוד עבודה: the verb and its noun share a root; the English keeps 'worship' for both, as the Hebrew does.
כמו שיכבד הנער את הזקן: the comparison gives the model of honour the author permits; the paragraph's argument turns on the difference between the two.
ואם אנשי לבב ... עשו זאת ... ברור הוא כי: the 'if' clause gives the case of the patriarchs and Joshua; the main clause is 'it is clear that'.
apparatus: Gen 18:2: the verse behind 'השתחווה ארצה לפני שלשה מלאכים' (Abraham bows to the ground before the three men).
Josh 5:13-14: the verse behind Joshua's falling to the ground before the man who stands before him.

segments.english: Second: the Jews are very careful in matters of other worship, and even to appear as one who honours it is forbidden to them. As they said in the Talmud and in the Rambam: "If a man turned aside from the road he was taking near a house of idolatry, and a thorn lodged in his foot, he may not bend, nor even kneel, nor bow down to remove it there, so that he should not appear in the eyes of passers-by as one who bows down and honours idolatry." And if the prostration before the Ark were like worship of another kind, the Jews would not have kept this custom; and since they kept it from the days of their fathers, it is a sign of truth that it is not corrupted.

grammar: כמו שאמרו בתלמוד וברמב"ם: the formula introduces a passage from the Talmud and the Rambam, given in the author's own wording; no reference is given.
לא ישח אף לא יכרע וישתחוה להוציאו: three verbs of bowing, two negated, the last joined to the purpose clause 'so that he should not appear'.
ואם היתה ... לא היו היהודים מחזיקים: a counterfactual, both clauses in the past; the author argues from what the Jews would not have done.
וכיון שהחזיקו בו מימי אבותיהם אות אמת הוא כי אינה משובשת: the argument from custom; 'since they kept it' is causal, and 'that it is not corrupted' gives the sign's content.
apparatus: The Talmud and Rambam passage is given in the author's own paraphrase; he names no tractate or chapter for it.
context: The Ark (הארון): the cabinet in the synagogue in which the Torah scrolls are kept; the custom the author describes is bowing before it.

segments.english: Third: one of the customs of honour by which they once honoured idolatry was kissing. So too we find in Scripture: "Yet I have left in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him." And it is said: "Those who sacrifice men kiss calves." If so, will all who kiss the Torah scroll be worshippers of idols? But the matter is not so, for this is only honour, that they honour their Torah, and not worship; and therefore the prostration before the Ark is also only honour and not worship.

grammar: וכן מצינו במקרא: the verse quoted is 1 Kgs 19:18, in the author's wording; 'we find' introduces it without a formula.
ונאמר זובחי אדם עגלים ישקון: the second verse, Hos 13:2; the subject is the sacrificers, and the verb is the plural 'kiss'.
ואם כן הוא יהיו כל המנשקים ... עובדי ע"ז?: a question about the future, answered by 'but this is not so'.
כי אין זה רק כבוד שיכבדו את תורתם ולא עבודה: 'for this is only honour, that they honour their Torah and not worship' explains 'this'.
apparatus: 1 Kgs 19:18: the verse quoted in the English, in the author's wording.
Hos 13:2: the verse quoted in the English.
context: Baal: the god of the Canaanites, whose worship Elijah opposed (1 Kgs 18); the verse the author quotes is set in that story.

segments.english: Fourth: experience has taught us that in all the languages of the nations customs of honour are found, by which a man honours his fellow when they meet, and so they bow their heads, one opposite the other, and this too has been for us a sign that it is not the worship of idols, but customs of honour.

grammar: הנסיון הורה אותנו: the subject is 'experience' and the verb is hiphil, 'taught us'.
יכבדו בם איש את רעהו בהיפגשם: 'by them' refers back to the customs; ב plus the infinitive with a suffix gives 'when they meet'.
וכן יכופו ראשיהם זה לעומת זה: 'one opposite the other' is the reciprocal phrase of the bowing.
והיה גם זה לנו לאות שאינה עבודת גלולים: the sign (אות) is the clause that follows: 'that it is not the worship of idols'.
